title: Header files
recap: A header provides a shared home for declarations needed by multiple source files. Including that header gives each translation unit consistent knowledge of the module's public functions.

Implementations normally remain in a paired source file, which should include its own header first. Each file should also include every library or project header required by the names it uses directly.
objectives: Place related function declarations in a project header.
Pair a header and source file using the same base name.
Use quotes for project headers and angle brackets for library headers.
Include a paired header from its implementation file.
Avoid dependence on accidental transitive includes.
warnings: Ordinary function definitions in widely included headers can violate the one-definition rule.
Header files are included by source files rather than listed as independent compiler inputs.
A .cpp implementation should be compiled, never included.
A source file should not rely on another header to include a dependency by accident.
challenge: Declare panelArea and totalArea in roof_math.h and define them in roof_math.cpp. In main.cpp, calculate the coverage of four panels that are each 12 feet by 10 feet and print the exact result.
hints: Start with the module boundary: roof_math.h tells callers which calculations exist, roof_math.cpp owns those calculations, and main.cpp uses the public declarations without seeing the implementations.

File flow in language-neutral pseudocode: in roof_math.h, publish panelArea(width, height) and totalArea(areaPerPanel, panelCount). In roof_math.cpp, load that interface; panelArea returns width multiplied by height, and totalArea returns areaPerPanel multiplied by panelCount. In main.cpp, load the interface and console-output support, calculate PANEL_AREA from 12 and 10, calculate COVERAGE from PANEL_AREA and 4, then print the required line.

Near-C++ structure: keep only two int-returning prototypes in the header; include that header first in roof_math.cpp and give both matching functions bodies with the appropriate multiplication expression; in main.cpp, keep the existing calls and send the final value through std::cout. Do not put either function body in the header or include a .cpp file.
